actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote. (text: CR H5282-5295)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 4465.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H5282-5295)
Mr. Schmidt moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Ordered to be Reported by Voice Vote.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal Inspectors General, advisory committees, judicial officers subject to financial disclosure, and federal prison inmates and staff through incorporated oversight provisions.
dimensions.evidence: amends chapters 4, 10, and 131 of title 5, United States Code

dimensions.assessment: Primarily codifies existing laws and technical corrections, though it incorporates major provisions such as federal prison inspections and judicial financial disclosure databases.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments only incorporate laws as described in subsection (a) to reflect existing law... and correct related technical errors.

dimensions.assessment: Suggests funding levels for prison oversight but notes provisions take effect upon the availability of specific appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: takes effect on the date that is 90 days after the date on which appropriations are made available

dimensions.assessment: Spans multiple chapters of Title 5, modifying rules for agency Inspectors General, Inspector General removal notifications, advisory committees, and federal prison oversight.
dimensions.evidence: To amend chapters 4, 10, and 131 of title 5, United States Code

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent statutory updates and codifications across multiple titles of federal law.
dimensions.evidence: To amend chapters 4, 10, and 131 of title 5, United States Code, as necessary to keep those chapters current

importance_detail.rationale: The bill updates Title 5 of the U.S. Code to incorporate post-October 2021 statutory amendments regarding Inspectors General, federal advisory committees, and government ethics, while making technical corrections and establishing a prison oversight and ombudsman regime.
